summary: Elliot Brandt is a 34-year-old analyst at the Tamsen County Assessor's Office on 12 weeks of parental leave. He is home at Marisol Gardens unit 209 with his son Theo, born July 19, and his wife Hana is still on maternity leave when the horizon opens. He treats fatherhood like a property-valuation model: tracking every ounce, nap and diaper in a spreadsheet and researching every rash and sleep regression at 3 a.m. He wants Theo sleeping in stretches longer than three hours. He would like to cook one real dinner, and he wants to go back to work in a way that doesn't leave Hana or Theo short. Pressing on him are his supervisor Brenda's emails about his return date and his mother Judith moving into the spare room in October. Hana goes back to work on November 3, which leaves him as the weekday parent. He jokes his way through all of it, and the jokes get thinner as the weeks go on.

impressions.statement: Turns every uncertainty into a research project, as if a big enough spreadsheet could make the baby predictable.

evidence.description: asks the assistant to build a heat-wave checklist with room temperatures and onesie layers per degree during the 100-degree days
pastes 9 days of nap times and asks for a regression analysis of wake windows
wants a weighted comparison matrix of four used crossovers, including rear-door opening angle
asks for a pros and cons table for two daycare centers with a column for 'vibe'

impressions.statement: Jokes about being incompetent so nobody notices how overwhelmed he actually is.

evidence.description: at 3 a.m. opens with 'rate my parenting: I put the diaper on backwards, twice' before asking whether bottle refusal is serious
calls himself 'Employee of the Month at Burnt Toast Inc.' while asking for a meal plan he can do one-handed
on Hana's second day back, writes 'day 2 solo, the baby is winning 14-0' and then asks how to get Theo to nap without being held
after the storm cancels his walk, says 'cool cool cool' and asks for indoor things to do with a four-month-old

impressions.statement: Avoids confronting his mother directly and quietly undoes what she changes instead.

evidence.description: asks for a 'gentle, non-offensive' way to say the mugs go back on the low shelf, then decides not to send it
asks how to relabel the fridge bins so they look like Judith's system 'but aren't'
drafts a text to Judith about not swaddling Theo anymore and asks the assistant to make it sound like Dr. Fong's idea
plans Sunday batch cooking for the weekends partly so Judith isn't there to rearrange it

impressions.statement: Quietly takes extra load off Hana and never explains why.

evidence.description: asks how to shift the 5 a.m. feed to himself too 'just for a while' without saying it's because she's exhausted
asks for a script to decline a visit from Hana's coworkers, saying she 'has a lot going on'
asks for lunch ideas he can pack for Hana the night before her first day back
schedules daycare tours on a day Hana's at work so she 'doesn't have to think about it'

impressions.statement: Is checked out from his job and doesn't care about going back.

evidence.description: lets Brenda's emails go unanswered for a week while Theo has his first cold, then asks for help catching up
asks for a summary of the new reassessment rules so he isn't behind in January
drafts transition notes for the colleague covering his appeal files
asks the assistant to quiz him on training module terms during Theo's nap

voice.texting_style: Mostly lowercase with full punctuation out of habit. Medium-length messages, more typos at night ('teh', 'bottel'). Dry self-deprecating jokes, an occasional 🙃, sometimes a sports metaphor.
voice.with_assistant: Gives a lot of context and often pastes spreadsheet rows or email text. Says please and thanks. Asks for tables and checklists, and likes long answers if they're structured, but at 3 a.m. he asks for 'the short version'.
quirks: Opens late-night messages with the time ('2:47 am update')
Scores parenting moments like baseball games
Apologizes to the assistant for typing one-handed
Rounds everything to ounces and minutes
